name: Gweike G2 20W Fiber
tagline: Desktop fiber marker for metal and select plastics
tldr: Gweike G2 packages a 20W fiber galvo in a desktop form factor. Solid option if you want metal marking with Gweike ecosystem familiarity from their CO₂ lines.
mainObjective: Entry fiber marking on small metal parts

priceRange.note: Official Gweike store, Oct 2026: $1,299 to $1,349 depending on manual or electric lift

engraveExample.description: Filled logo on stainless steel plate

pros: Cheapest way into the G2 line: $1,349 with the 150 mm lens and electric lift (Gweike US store, Oct 2026)
Light enough to move around (about 6.5 kg per Gweike) and usable handheld for parts that do not fit under the head
Enough power for surface marking of steel, brass, anodized aluminum and many plastics
cons: Slowest of the line for depth: about 2.1 mm in brass after two hours of passes in Gweike's own test
Thin-sheet cut-outs are slow: 11 trips over a 0.5 mm brass sheet at 10 mm/s (Gweike demo)
Q-switched source, not MOPA: limited colour control on stainless steel

faq.question: How deep can the G2 20W engrave into brass?
faq.answer: In Gweike's comparison video, two hours of repeated passes at 1,000 mm/s reached about 2.1 mm in brass, and one hour reached about 1.7 mm in slate. Everyday marking (serial numbers, logos, QR codes) only needs a few hundredths of a millimetre, which the 20W does quickly; millimetre-deep relief is slow at this power.

faq.question: Can the G2 20W cut thin metal sheet?
faq.answer: Only very thin stock, and slowly. Gweike's demo cuts 0.5 mm brass at 10 mm/s in 11 passes. Treat it as an occasional cut-out tool for small tags and blanks, not as a sheet cutter.

faq.question: Is the 20W enough, or should I pay more for the G2 Pro?
faq.answer: The 20W lists at $1,349 with the 150 mm lens and electric lift on Gweike's US store (October 2026); the manual-lift 110 mm version at $1,299 was sold out. It covers pet tags, tumblers, tools and anodized aluminum. If you expect deep engraving, coins or regular thin-sheet cut-outs, the Pro saves a lot of passes. Neither is a MOPA source, so colour marking on steel stays limited.

standoutFeatures.title: Lowest entry price in the G2 line
standoutFeatures.body: At $1,349 with the 150 mm lens and electric lift (October 2026), the 20W costs about $450 less than the same G2 Pro configuration. The difference pays for the $129 roller rotary and part of a fume extractor.

standoutFeatures.title: Gentle power for fine marks
standoutFeatures.body: Lower power makes it easier to mark plated items, anodized layers and plastics without over-burning, and test grids converge quickly. Gweike lists a 0.1 mm minimum character size for the G2 series.

beginnerNotes: This profile is the 20W SKU on Gweike G2 Fiber. Read the TL;DR and benchmarks above, then compare other power options via the chips before buying.
proTips: Fix parts firmly; start with low power test squares on scrap metal. Rotary adds complexity: budget time to learn indexing.
primaryUse: Desktop fiber marking for jewelry-scale and test jobs

editorialDepth.advantages: Gweike G2 Fiber 20W fits shops that mark stainless, aluminum, and tools daily without a CO₂ bay. A solid bench option for jewelry, tags, and small batches.
editorialDepth.limitations: Skip if wood, leather, or cast acrylic pay your bills. Deep metal cutting and large industrial panels often need more fiber headroom (30W or 50W) or a different machine class.
